title: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy with Negative JC Virus PCR following Treatment of Follicular Lymphoma: Implications for Biologics in the Era of Targeted Cancer Therapy
case_prompt: A 69-year-old man with stage IIIB follicular lymphoma, atrial fibrillation, and pulmonary sarcoidosis presented with two months of progressive dysarthria and right-sided weakness. He had completed six cycles of rituximab and bendamustine one year earlier for lymphoma. MRI of the brain showed multiple confluent T2-weighted FLAIR hyperintensities in the inferior frontal lobes and left corona radiata, and vascular imaging demonstrated no flow-limiting stenosis, occlusion, or aneurysm. Admission laboratory tests, including CBC, metabolic panel, rheumatologic markers (ANA negative; ANCA titer <1:20; complement C3 and C4 normal), inflammatory markers (CRP 0.16 mg/dL; ESR 17 mm/hr), and ACE level (27 mcg/L), were within normal limits. HIV and HCV screens were nonreactive; immunoglobulin levels were normal; syphilis and Lyme serologies were negative. Evaluation for lymphoma recurrence—including beta2-microglobulin, LDH, PET scan, and skin biopsy—revealed no evidence of disease. Lumbar puncture showed clear fluid with normal cell counts, glucose of 57 mg/dL, protein of 38 mg/dL, nonreactive VDRL, and negative JC virus PCR (<500 copies/mL). Empirical high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone yielded no improvement. A repeat MRI showed mild enlargement of nonenhancing confluent subcortical and periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the left corona radiata and right temporal lobe with associated restricted diffusion and scattered punctate enhancement.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. A cerebrovascular event was considered given the focal deficits, but angiography ruled out stenosis or occlusion — “There was no flow-limiting stenosis, occlusion, or aneurysm.”  
2. CNS lymphoma recurrence was suspected due to his oncologic history, but PET imaging showed no active lesions — “PET scan revealed no hypermetabolic lesions in the brain to suggest recurrence of his lymphoma.”  
3. Vasculitic or inflammatory disorders were entertained because of confluent white-matter changes, but serologic markers were unremarkable — “ANA was negative, ANCA titer was < 1 : 20, complement C3 was 104 mg/dL (within normal limits), and complement C4 was 23 mg/dL (within normal limits).”  
4. Neurosarcoidosis was in the differential given his sarcoidosis, but ACE was normal — “ACE level of 27 mcg/L (within normal limits).”  
5. JC virus–mediated PML was considered due to immunosuppression and MRI appearance, but initial CSF PCR was negative — “CSF PCR was negative for JC virus PCR (<500 copies/mL).”  
6. PML was confirmed by neuropathology demonstrating viral inclusions and immunostaining — “SV40 stain positivity confirming JC virus infection.”
